docs.title: Known risks
docs.text:
• Harness formats change often. M7 re-verifies each one against its docs, and snapshot tests catch drift.
  • Sandboxing differs by OS. Landlock needs Linux 5.13 or later (ADR-0007), and macOS sandbox-exec is deprecated but still works. doctor must report the fallback clearly.
  • RN screenshots depend on Expo web or a simulator. The engine degrades to "no screenshot" with a clear message.
  • Live GitHub surprises: the live runs caught 4 bugs the fakes missed (ADR-0018/19/23). Every milestone that touches GitHub ends with a live check.

docs.title: Data Policy
docs.text: ehai scans what it writes — tracker items, PRDs, POC mock data, reports — and surfaces or blocks sensitive data before it lands anywhere. The behavior is configurable per team and per domain.

docs.title: Domain profiles
docs.text:
The guard uses additive profiles. The tech profile is always the base; each other profile adds domain-specific patterns on top.

Profile What it detects tech (default) SSN/national IDs, email, phone, street address, date of birth health + tech · medical record numbers (MRN), insurance/member IDs, name near medical terms finance + tech · credit card numbers (Luhn-validated), IBAN, US bank routing numbers gdpr + tech · EU passport patterns, data-subject language (consent, right to erasure)

docs.title: Modes
docs.text: Mode Behavior off No scanning. Write anything. warn (default) Surface findings and ask: redact / keep / cancel before writing. strict High-confidence findings are auto-redacted. Low-confidence findings are surfaced. Never writes suspicious data silently.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
# ~/.ehai/config.toml
[compliance]
mode    = "warn"    # off | warn | strict
profile = "tech"    # tech | health | finance | gdpr

Change at any time — takes effect on the next tool call. No restart needed.

docs.title: Custom patterns
docs.text:
Append extra patterns after the profile rules:

[compliance]
mode    = "warn"
profile = "tech"
patterns = [
  { name = "employee-id", regex = "\\bEMP-\\d{6}\\b" },
  { name = "project-code", regex = "\\bPROJ-[A-Z]{3}-\\d{4}\\b" },
]

Custom patterns are matched with the same confidence logic as built-in rules. name becomes the finding kind shown in redaction notices: [REDACTED:employee-id].

docs.title: Audit log
docs.text:
Every compliance decision is appended to ~/.ehai/audit/ as newline-delimited JSON:

{
  "ts": "2026-11-18T10:23:01Z",
  "command": "save_prd",
  "action": "redact",
  "findings": [{ "kind": "email", "count": 2 }]
}

Values are never logged

The audit log records kinds and counts only — never the actual sensitive values. ehai guard-check "<text>" echoes findings to your terminal but never writes the content to any file.

docs.title: Changing profile mid-session
docs.text:
ehai config set compliance.profile health

Or set it once in ~/.ehai/config.toml. A repo-level .ehai.toml can override the global setting for a specific project.

docs.title: Checking a string manually
docs.text:
ehai guard-check "SSN: 123-45-6789 and email jane@example.com"
# findings: ssn ×1, email ×1

Useful for testing a custom pattern before writing it to config.

docs.title: How ehai works
docs.text:
This page covers why ehai exists, what problem it solves, the ideas behind it, how it is built, and how a request moves through it, with diagrams.

Diagram colour key: used the same way on every diagram below.

flowchart LR
  U["👤 People"]:::user --> H["🤖 AI harness"]:::harness --> E["⚙️ ehai engine"]:::engine --> X["🌐 External service"]:::ext
  E --> S["💾 Local state"]:::store
  E --> G["🛡️ Safety / guard"]:::guard
  classDef user fill:#f97316,stroke:#c2410c,color:#fff
  classDef harness fill:#2563eb,stroke:#1e40af,color:#fff
  classDef engine fill:#7c3aed,stroke:#5b21b6,color:#fff
  classDef ext fill:#16a34a,stroke:#166534,color:#fff
  classDef store fill:#0891b2,stroke:#155e75,color:#fff
  classDef guard fill:#dc2626,stroke:#991b1b,color:#fff

docs.title: 1. The problem
docs.text:
AI coding assistants made writing code fast. Everything around the code is still slow and manual:

Pain Who feels it What it costs Requirements live in docs and chats; someone retypes them into the tracker by hand PM Hours per feature, lost detail, duplicate issues Every AI tool (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI…) needs its own setup, prompts and conventions Developers Inconsistent output; the team cannot share one workflow A developer jumps between tracker, terminal and AI chat to start a task, open a PR and move the card Developers Context switching; stale boards Trying a UI idea means a branch in the real repo, and a fresh worktree will not run (no .env, no deps, port clashes) PM + Dev Prototypes are slow, risky to main, or never built Prototypes ignore the app's real colors, fonts and components PM POCs look nothing like the product, so feedback is poor Someone pastes a customer email or ID into a ticket Everyone Compliance incidents The AI asks the same questions every session Everyone It never learns how this team works

docs.title: 2. How ehai helps
docs.text:
ehai is one engine that every AI harness talks to. It turns the AI from a code generator into a full SDLC teammate:

flowchart LR
  idea["💡 Idea"]:::user --> prd["📄 PRD<br/>/ehai:plan"]:::engine
  prd --> bd["🗂️ Breakdown<br/>epics → stories → tasks<br/>/ehai:breakdown"]:::engine
  bd --> board["📋 GitHub Project<br/>/ehai:sync"]:::ext
  board --> assign["👥 Owners<br/>/ehai:assign"]:::harness
  board --> status["📊 Status report<br/>/ehai:status"]:::user
  board --> triage["🐞 Bugs and requests<br/>/ehai:triage"]:::harness
  bd -. "try the UI first" .-> poc["🧪 POC worktree<br/>ehai poc new"]:::engine
  poc -. "promote on request" .-> pr["🔀 PR to main<br/>ehai poc promote"]:::ext
  classDef user fill:#f97316,stroke:#c2410c,color:#fff
  classDef harness fill:#2563eb,stroke:#1e40af,color:#fff
  classDef engine fill:#7c3aed,stroke:#5b21b6,color:#fff
  classDef ext fill:#16a34a,stroke:#166534,color:#fff
  • PMs go from idea → PRD → approved tasks on the board in one conversation, in the Claude desktop app or Claude Code, without terminal commands.
  • Developers see their tasks, with acceptance criteria, on the board and get assigned with /ehai:assign, from whichever AI tool they like. Automating branches, PR text and card moves (/ehai:start, /ehai:pr, /ehai:done) is planned.
  • Everyone can ask for a UI prototype that uses the app's own design system and runs in an isolated copy of the repo, so main is never touched.
  • The guard checks every tracker write, PRD and mock-data fixture for sensitive data first.
  • Preferences make each session a little better than the last.

docs.title: 3. Philosophy
docs.text:
These rules decide every design trade-off in ehai.

Principle What it means in practice One engine, thin adapters All logic is in one Rust binary. Each harness gets only generated config and prompt files that call the same MCP tools, so a new AI tool costs one small adapter, not a rewrite. Main is sacred POCs live in separate worktrees on ehai/poc/... branches outside the repo. Nothing is merged, pushed or promoted unless you ask. Never break, always run Atomic updates with automatic rollback, versioned config with migrations, additive-only MCP schemas, and a per-request panic guard so one bad call never kills the server. Ask, don't guess Questions go through the harness's native multiple-choice UI. Anything that can be detected is detected instead of asked. Every question has a default. Learn and adapt Observed choices become preferences, which become defaults. Explicit statements always beat observations, and the user can edit or delete any of them. Safe by default Data guard on every write, sandboxed agent work, secrets never sent to the tracker, logs or the LLM (keys only, never values). Minimal footprint One static binary. No Node, Python or Docker to run it. No telemetry. ehai uninstall leaves no traces. Role-aware Same commands for everyone; PMs get plain language and visuals, developers get paths, diffs and commands.

docs.title: 4.1 Architecture
docs.text:
flowchart TB
  subgraph people["People"]
    pm["👩‍💼 PM"]:::user
    dev["👨‍💻 Developer"]:::user

docs.title: 5.1 One tool call, end to end
docs.text:
The harness spawns ehai mcp per session. The engine loads your preferences, runs the tool, checks it with the guard, writes, and records what it learned.

sequenceDiagram
  autonumber
  actor U as 👤 User
  participant H as 🤖 AI harness
  participant M as ⚙️ ehai MCP server
  participant P as 💾 Prefs store
  participant G as 🛡️ Guard
  participant T as 🌐 Tracker

  U->>H: /ehai:sync
  H->>M: spawn "ehai mcp" (stdio)
  rect rgba(124, 58, 237, 0.15)
    H->>M: read resource ehai://prefs
    M->>P: load user + repo prefs
    P-->>M: compact preference block
    M-->>H: role, style, defaults
  end
  H->>M: call tool sync_plan
  rect rgba(220, 38, 38, 0.15)

  else sensitive data found

docs.title: 5.2 The agent loop (needs_input)
docs.text:
ehai never guesses on a decision that belongs to the user. When a tool cannot continue on its own, it returns a structured question instead of failing. The harness shows it in its native multiple-choice UI and calls the same tool again with the answer.

flowchart TD
  start(["User asks for something"]):::user --> plan["🤖 Harness picks a skill<br/>and loads ehai://prefs"]:::harness
  plan --> tool["Call ehai MCP tool"]:::harness
  tool --> run["⚙️ Engine runs the step"]:::engine
  run --> check{"Can it finish<br/>without a decision?"}:::engine
  check -- "yes" --> guard{"🛡️ Guard passes?"}:::guard
  check -- "no" --> ni["Return needs_input<br/>question · options · retry_param"]:::engine
  guard -- "yes" --> write["Write to tracker / repo / worktree"]:::ext
  guard -- "no (warn / strict)" --> ni
  ni --> ask["❓ Harness asks with native<br/>multiple-choice UI"]:::harness
  ask --> ans(["User picks an option"]):::user
  ans -- "retry_param = choice" --> tool
  write --> learn["💾 Record observation in prefs"]:::store
  learn --> reply["Role-aware answer<br/>+ next options"]:::harness
  reply --> more{"More to do?"}:::user
  more -- "yes" --> plan
  more -- "no" --> stop(["Done"]):::user

  classDef harness fill:#2563eb,stroke:#1e40af,color:#fff

  classDef store fill:#0891b2,stroke:#155e75,color:#fff
  classDef guard fill:#dc2626,stroke:#991b1b,color:#fff

Because the loop goes through MCP, it works the same in every harness. Clients that support MCP elicitation get the question directly; others render the needs_input result.

docs.title: 6. Preferences: how ehai learns
docs.text:
Each tool call can record an observation. Observations build confidence over time and become defaults; anything you state explicitly always wins.

flowchart TD

  obs --> store[("💾 Prefs store<br/>user.toml · project.toml")]:::store
  exp --> store
  store --> conf["Confidence<br/>↑ reinforced · ↓ contradicted · ↓ decays over time"]:::engine
  conf --> resolve{"Resolve per key"}:::engine
  resolve --> inject["ehai://prefs → compact<br/>'User preferences' block"]:::harness
  inject --> out["Better defaults,<br/>fewer questions,<br/>role-aware output"]:::ext
  out --> act

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text: Zero to your first /ehai:plan in about 5 minutes.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
Needed For Notes macOS 12+, Windows 10 1809+, or Linux 5.13+ (x86_64 or arm64; Windows x86_64) everything One static binary, no runtime to install curl, tar and sha256sum or shasum installer Already on macOS and almost every Linux. Windows uses built-in PowerShell git 2.20+ POCs, worktrees ehai doctor checks it gh or a GITHUB_TOKEN GitHub Projects tracker ehai reuses gh auth token; without gh, set GITHUB_TOKEN (or GH_TOKEN). Not needed for the local tracker Chrome / Chromium optional POC screenshots only; skipped if missing Your project's own tools (pnpm/npm/yarn/bun, go, uv/poetry/pip) optional Only to install dependencies and run previews inside POC worktrees

Not needed: Node, Python, Docker or minisign (the installer gets a temporary copy to check the signature).

docs.title: 1. Install
docs.text:
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jagadeeshm007/ehai/main/install/install.sh | sh

This downloads the right binary for your OS and architecture, verifies the checksum and minisign signature, installs to ~/.ehai/bin, and adds it to your PATH.

ehai works in the same terminal straight away, so you don't need to reload your shell or open a new terminal:

  • macOS / Linux: besides adding ~/.ehai/bin to your shell rc (for new terminals), the installer links ehai into a folder that's already on your PATH and writable without sudo: ~/.local/bin, ~/bin, /opt/homebrew/bin or /usr/local/bin. It never replaces a file that isn't its own. If none of those is available, it prints the one line to paste instead (export PATH="$HOME/.ehai/bin:$PATH").
  • Windows: the installer also adds ehai to the current PowerShell session's PATH.

The setup wizard shows which keys to press next to every question: ↑/↓ to move, Space to select or unselect in multi-choice lists, Enter to confirm, Esc to go back.

You don't need minisign installed. If it's missing, the installer downloads a temporary copy of the official build (pinned by SHA-256), uses it to check the signature, and deletes it. If that download fails, it warns and still checks the SHA-256 checksum. Set EHAI_REQUIRE_SIGNATURE=1 to stop the install instead.

Which version gets installed: the newest stable release. If there isn't one yet, the newest beta, then the newest alpha. To choose yourself:

# a channel: alpha | beta | stable
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jagadeeshm007/ehai/main/install/install.sh | EHAI_CHANNEL=beta sh
# an exact version
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jagadeeshm007/ehai/main/install/install.sh | EHAI_VERSION=v0.1.0-alpha.2 sh

On Windows, set $env:EHAI_CHANNEL or $env:EHAI_VERSION before running the install line. If GitHub can't be reached, the installer says so and prints a link to download by hand: that version's release page if you set EHAI_VERSION, otherwise the repo's main branch.

docs.title: 2. Init
docs.text:
ehai init

The wizard runs automatic detection (spinner per check), shows a summary card of what it found, then asks at most 5 questions:

Question Default Your role PM + Dev Harnesses to wire up auto-detected, pre-checked Tracker GitHub Projects (or local if no gh) Data policy mode warn Sandbox mode restricted

It applies each step with a live checklist and shows the three most useful commands for your role at the end.

No GitHub account?

Choose local tracker at the tracker question. All PM flows work offline. Add GitHub later with ehai tracker set github.

docs.title: 3. Open your project
docs.text:
cd my-app

The first time ehai runs in a repo it detects the stack (React Native, Vite, Next.js, Go, Python, etc.), reads design tokens, and writes .ehai/profile.toml. You'll see a one-screen summary and a confirm prompt.

docs.title: 4. Plan something
docs.text:
In Claude Code (or any connected harness):

/ehai:plan A settings screen where users can toggle notification preferences

ehai interviews you with multiple-choice questions, then produces a full PRD — problem statement, user flows (Mermaid), success metrics, risks — and runs a gap-finder loop to deepen it before handing off to breakdown.

docs.title: 5. Break it down and sync
docs.text:
/ehai:breakdown
/ehai:sync

breakdown turns the PRD into epics → stories → tasks with Given/When/Then acceptance criteria. It shows a board preview and waits for your approval before syncing. sync pushes to your tracker idempotently — running it twice never duplicates items.

docs.title: 6. Pick up a task
docs.text:
/ehai:assign I'll take #12

Assigns #12 to you on the board. Automating the branch, PR text and card moves (/ehai:start, /ehai:pr, /ehai:done) is planned.

docs.title: Setup & Connections
docs.text: This guide walks through every connection ehai needs: GitHub auth, harness wiring, and optional services.

docs.title: GitHub
docs.text: ehai needs a GitHub token with project scope to manage GitHub Projects v2 — creating fields, syncing items, linking PRs, and reading team members.

docs.title: Option A: gh CLI
docs.text:
# Install gh if you don't have it
# macOS:  brew install gh
# Linux:  https://cli.github.com/manual/installation
# Windows: winget install gh

gh auth login                     # first-time login (browser flow)
gh auth refresh -s project        # add project scope to an existing session

ehai reads the token via gh auth token automatically. No config needed.

docs.title: Option B: env var
docs.text:
export GITHUB_TOKEN=ghp_xxxxxxxxxxxx   # or GH_TOKEN — either works

Add to your shell's RC file to persist it. ehai picks up either variable.

docs.title: Option C: no GitHub account
docs.text:
At ehai init, choose local tracker when asked. All PM flows, PRD storage, breakdown, and status work fully offline. Add GitHub later:

ehai tracker set github    # prompts for auth if needed

docs.title: Verify
docs.text:
ehai doctor
# ✔ GitHub auth (jagadeeshm007, project scope)
# ✔ tracker reachable (My Project · 23 items)

If you see a scope error:

gh auth refresh -s project

docs.title: Harnesses
docs.text: Connect ehai to any AI coding harness. ehai init wires everything automatically — use the commands below to connect or reconnect a specific harness.

docs.title: Claude Code
docs.text:
Claude Code connects via MCP over stdio. After ehai init this is wired automatically as a user-scope MCP server.

ehai connect claude-code

# Or directly with the claude CLI:
claude mcp add --scope user ehai -- ehai mcp

Verify — open Claude Code and run /ehai:help. It calls the ping tool, says whether ehai is connected, and lists the commands.

Troubleshoot:

ehai doctor                       # checks adapter status
ehai adapters list                # shows all adapters + detect result
ehai disconnect claude-code       # clean disconnect
ehai connect claude-code          # reconnect

docs.title: Claude Desktop
docs.text:
Claude Desktop uses skills (.zip) + MCP connector.

ehai connect claude-desktop

This writes the MCP server entry to your claude_desktop_config.json and generates a skills ZIP at ~/.ehai/adapters/claude-desktop/ehai-skills.zip.

Then in Claude Desktop: Settings → Skills → Upload ZIP.

PM on Claude Desktop

PMs get the full planning flow — PRD generation, breakdown, sync — without touching a terminal. The skills ZIP includes PM-optimised prompts with visual-first output (Mermaid diagrams, tables).

docs.title: Codex CLI
docs.text:
ehai connect codex

Writes to ~/.codex/config.toml under [mcp_servers] and places prompt files in ~/.codex/prompts/.

docs.title: Gemini CLI
docs.text:
ehai connect gemini

Writes to ~/.gemini/settings.json under mcpServers and places TOML command files in ~/.gemini/commands/.

docs.title: Cursor
docs.text:
ehai connect cursor

Writes to ~/.cursor/mcp.json and places rule files in ~/.cursor/rules/.

docs.title: VS Code / GitHub Copilot
docs.text:
ehai connect vscode

Writes to VS Code's user mcp.json (under servers key) and places prompt files in the VS Code prompts directory.

docs.title: OpenCode
docs.text:
ehai connect opencode

Writes to ~/.config/opencode/config.json and places prompt files in the opencode commands directory.

docs.title: Windsurf
docs.text:
ehai connect windsurf

Writes to ~/.codeium/windsurf/mcp_server_config.json and places workflow files.

docs.title: Any other harness
docs.text:
ehai connect agents-md

Writes a reference card to ~/AGENTS.md describing ehai's MCP server config and all available slash commands. Any harness that reads AGENTS.md picks this up automatically.

docs.title: OpenAI-compatible APIs
docs.text:
ehai's engine makes no LLM calls itself — all reasoning happens inside your harness. If your harness connects to an OpenAI-compatible endpoint (Azure OpenAI, Ollama, LM Studio, Groq, etc.):

  1. Configure your harness's model/API endpoint as usual.
  2. Run ehai connect <harness> to wire up MCP.
  3. Use /ehai:plan, /ehai:sync, etc. — the harness calls ehai's MCP tools the same way regardless of model.

docs.title: Managing connections
docs.text:
ehai adapters list                 # show all adapters: detected / installed / status
ehai adapters regenerate           # re-render all installed adapters (after rename or update)
ehai disconnect cursor             # remove one adapter
ehai disconnect --all              # remove all adapters
ehai adapters install vscode       # install a specific adapter
ehai adapters remove opencode      # remove a specific adapter

docs.title: First-time repo setup
docs.text:
The first time any ehai command runs in a repo, it detects:

  • Stack (React Native, Vite, Next.js, Go, Python, pnpm monorepo, etc.)
  • Design tokens (Tailwind config, CSS variables, MUI/NativeWind themes)
  • Conventions (naming, test framework, commit style, branch naming)
  • Existing tracker fields and label sets

It shows a one-screen summary and asks to confirm, then writes .ehai/profile.toml. Rerun anytime:

ehai repo init

docs.title: Disconnect one harness
docs.text:
Remove ehai from a single AI harness without touching anything else:

ehai disconnect claude-code     # unregisters MCP, removes generated files
ehai disconnect cursor
ehai disconnect --all           # removes every connected harness at once

ehai only removes the files it generated (inside its own # >>> ehai >>> block or dedicated config key). Your own edits to those files are preserved.

docs.title: Remove ehai from a repo
docs.text:
ehai writes one directory per repo: .ehai/ at the repo root. It contains the detected stack profile, local plan cache, and optional POC manifest. It is never required for the binary to run.

# From inside the repo:
rm -rf .ehai/

If you committed .ehai/profile.toml to share conventions with the team, also remove it from git:

git rm -r .ehai/
git commit -m "chore: remove ehai repo profile"

Nothing else in the repo is touched by ehai (no changes to package.json, go.mod, etc.).

docs.title: Full uninstall
docs.text:
Remove ehai completely from your machine — binary, config, prefs, adapters, logs, cached data, and PATH entries:

ehai uninstall

This asks for confirmation, then:

  • Disconnects every harness (ehai disconnect --all)
  • Deletes ~/.ehai/ contents: config.toml, prefs/, adapters/, bin/, logs/, audit/, cache/, worktrees/, ports.json
  • Removes the export PATH line (or fish equivalent) from your shell RC files
  • Removes the ehai link the installer put in a folder on your PATH (~/.local/bin, /usr/local/bin, …), only if it points into ~/.ehai
  • If you saved a token at ~/.ehai/token, that file is deleted too

Repo profiles (.ehai/ inside your repos) are not deleted — remove those manually per repo if needed.

To skip the confirmation prompt (CI or scripting):

ehai uninstall --yes

docs.title: Device migration
docs.text:
Move your ehai setup to a new machine:

# Old machine
ehai migration export                     # → ehai-backup-20261118.zip

# New machine (after installing ehai)
ehai migration import ehai-backup-*.zip   # restores config, prefs, local tracker
ehai adapters regenerate                  # re-wires harnesses with new paths

The ZIP contains your config, preferences, and local tracker data. Harness adapter files are excluded because they contain machine-specific absolute paths — adapters regenerate rebuilds them correctly.

docs.title: Build with spec-driven tools, run it with ehai
docs.text:
Spec-driven tools are good at creating software. You describe what you want, they turn it into requirements, a design, tasks and code, and they stop for your approval along the way. Once the code exists, most of the work is running and improving it:

  • keeping the team's board up to date,
  • triaging bugs,
  • knowing what is blocked,
  • trying improvements safely before committing to them.

ehai covers that second part. Use a spec tool to create the project or each big feature, then use ehai on top to track it, maintain it, and prototype improvements.

flowchart LR
  idea(["💡 Idea"]):::user --> spec["📐 Spec tool<br/>AI-DLC · Spec Kit · Kiro<br/>requirements → design → tasks → code"]:::harness
  spec --> handoff["🔁 Hand off to ehai<br/>/ehai:plan · /ehai:breakdown"]:::engine
  handoff --> board["📋 GitHub Project<br/>/ehai:sync"]:::ext
  board --> run["🛠️ Maintain<br/>/ehai:status · /ehai:triage · /ehai:assign"]:::engine
  run --> poc["🧪 Improve safely<br/>ehai poc new · run · compare"]:::engine
  poc -- "winner becomes the next spec" --> spec
  poc -- "small change: promote" --> pr["🔀 PR"]:::ext
  classDef user fill:#f97316,stroke:#c2410c,color:#fff
  classDef harness fill:#2563eb,stroke:#1e40af,color:#fff
  classDef engine fill:#7c3aed,stroke:#5b21b6,color:#fff
  classDef ext fill:#16a34a,stroke:#166534,color:#fff

docs.title: Who does what
docs.text:
Job Spec tool ehai Turn an idea into requirements, design and tasks ✅ main job /ehai:plan for smaller features Write the code from the spec ✅ — Put the work on the team's board, without duplicates on re-sync — ✅ /ehai:sync Progress, blockers, stale items, risks — ✅ /ehai:status Bugs and requests after launch Spec Kit bug flow, AI-DLC bugfix scope ✅ /ehai:triage puts them on the board, checking for duplicates first Who works on what — ✅ /ehai:assign Try UI ideas without touching main — ✅ ehai poc (isolated worktree, real design tokens, own ports) Keep sensitive data out of tickets — ✅ data policy guard on every write Learn how your team works AI-DLC learnings, Spec Kit constitution ✅ preferences (/ehai:prefs)

Both work through the same AI tool (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot and others), so you don't switch apps. The spec tool brings its own slash commands, and ehai adds /ehai: commands and MCP tools next to them.

How the hand-off works

ehai doesn't parse these tools' files itself. You point /ehai:plan or /ehai:breakdown at them, and the AI reads them and fills ehai's PRD and breakdown, which ehai checks (every metric has a number, every story has Given/When/Then, no dependency cycles) before saving. Run it again after the spec changes: ehai updates existing tracker items in place instead of creating duplicates.

docs.title: Pick a spec tool
docs.text:
Tool Best for You get AWS AI-DLC Teams that want a full, audited lifecycle with approval gates; brownfield and enterprise work Phases from ideation to operation, 11 scopes (e.g. mvp, feature, bugfix, poc, refactor, express), expert agents, an audit trail. Works with Claude Code, Kiro, Codex, Cursor, opencode and Copilot GitHub Spec Kit Lightweight, file-based specs per feature A constitution, then spec.md → plan.md → tasks.md per feature, then implement and converge Kiro specs Teams already using Kiro requirements.md (EARS: "WHEN … THE SYSTEM SHALL …"), design.md, and implementation tasks per feature

Any other tool that writes requirements and tasks as files works the same way: point /ehai:plan and /ehai:breakdown at its files.

Checked 2026-11-19

These tools change quickly. The commands below match their docs on that date. If one doesn't work, check the tool's own README.

docs.title: Recipe 1: AWS AI-DLC + ehai
docs.text:
1. Install AI-DLC and connect it to your AI tool (from the project root):

curl -fsSL https://github.com/awslabs/aidlc-workflows/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sh
aidlc config --harness claude      # or kiro, codex, cursor, opencode, copilot
aidlc doctor

2. Build the project with AI-DLC. Describe it; AI-DLC picks a scope and walks you through each stage, asking for approval before moving on:

/aidlc Build a booking app for small clinics: patients book, staff manage the calendar

Its requirements, user stories, designs and decisions are saved under aidlc/spaces/<space>/intents/<YYMMDD>-<label>/.

3. Hand off to ehai once Inception (requirements and stories) is approved. You don't need to wait for the code:

/ehai:plan Use the AI-DLC requirements and user stories in aidlc/spaces/default/intents/<record>/ as the source. Only ask me about gaps.
/ehai:breakdown <prd-slug>   Keep AI-DLC's story ids and Given/When/Then criteria.
/ehai:sync

AI-DLC's stories already use Given/When/Then, so they map straight onto ehai stories. AI-DLC's units of work become epics.

4. Track while AI-DLC builds. AI-DLC's Construction phase writes the code; ehai keeps the board in step:

/ehai:status            # % done per epic, blocked and stale items
/ehai:assign t12 to priya

5. Maintain and improve with the improvement loop below. For a bigger next feature, start a new AI-DLC intent (/aidlc --scope feature …) and hand it off again.

docs.title: Recipe 2: GitHub Spec Kit + ehai
docs.text:
1. Install Spec Kit and start a project:

uv tool install specify-cli
specify init my-app --integration copilot   # or your AI tool, see Spec Kit's integrations list

2. Specify and plan a feature in your AI tool:

/speckit-constitution   Code quality, testing and accessibility rules for this project
/speckit-specify        Patients can book, move and cancel appointments online
/speckit-clarify        (optional) resolve open questions
/speckit-plan           React + Go API, Postgres
/speckit-tasks

This writes the feature's spec.md, plan.md and tasks.md (plus research.md, data-model.md and contracts/ when needed). Spec Kit keeps track of the active feature folder in .specify/feature.json.

3. Put it on the board with ehai before implementing, so the team sees progress from day one:

/ehai:plan Use the active Spec Kit feature's spec.md as the source. Only ask me about gaps.
/ehai:breakdown <prd-slug>   Use the Spec Kit tasks.md as the task list; keep its task ids and order.
/ehai:sync

4. Implement with Spec Kit, track with ehai:

/speckit-implement
/speckit-converge      # repeat implement + converge until it reports Converged
/ehai:status

5. Next feature: run /speckit-specify again, then /ehai:plan → /ehai:breakdown → /ehai:sync. Bugs found later go through /ehai:triage, which checks the board for duplicates first.

docs.title: Recipe 3: Kiro specs + ehai
docs.text:
1. Create a spec in Kiro. It writes requirements.md, design.md and the implementation tasks for the feature, typically under .kiro/specs/<feature>/.

  2. Hand off to ehai. Kiro has no ehai adapter yet, so pick one of these:

    • From another AI tool with ehai installed (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor…), open the same repo and run:

      /ehai:plan Use .kiro/specs/<feature>/requirements.md as the source. Turn each EARS requirement into an acceptance criterion.
/ehai:breakdown <prd-slug>   Use the Kiro tasks as the task list.
/ehai:sync

    • Inside Kiro, add ehai's MCP server to Kiro's MCP settings (command ehai, args ["mcp"], the same snippet as in AGENTS.md). Then ask in chat: "Use ehai to save a PRD and breakdown from this spec, then sync it." The agent calls ehai's save_prd, save_breakdown and sync_plan tools directly.

docs.title: The improvement loop
docs.text:
After launch, most changes are improvements to something that already works. Try them as POCs first: each POC is an isolated copy of the repo with your real colors, fonts and components, its own .env and ports, and it never touches main.

flowchart TD
  fb(["📣 Feedback, bug or idea"]):::user --> tri["/ehai:triage<br/>classified, deduplicated,<br/>on the board"]:::engine
  tri --> size{"How big?"}:::user
  size -- "a UI or UX change" --> new["ehai poc new feature 'idea'<br/>isolated worktree, own ports"]:::engine
  new --> try["ehai poc run feature n<br/>no cd needed"]:::harness
  try --> iter["ehai poc iterate feature n 'feedback'"]:::engine
  iter --> cmp["ehai poc compare feature 1 2"]:::engine
  cmp --> pick{"Keep one?"}:::user
  pick -- "small, ready" --> promote["ehai poc promote feature n<br/>opens a PR after you confirm"]:::ext
  pick -- "big, needs a spec" --> respec["Spec tool: new feature spec<br/>using the winning POC as reference"]:::harness
  respec --> hand["/ehai:plan → /ehai:breakdown → /ehai:sync"]:::engine
  pick -- "none" --> discard["ehai poc discard feature n<br/>archived as a tag"]:::store
  size -- "a new capability" --> respec
  classDef user fill:#f97316,stroke:#c2410c,color:#fff
  classDef harness fill:#2563eb,stroke:#1e40af,color:#fff
  classDef engine fill:#7c3aed,stroke:#5b21b6,color:#fff
  classDef ext fill:#16a34a,stroke:#166534,color:#fff
  classDef store fill:#0891b2,stroke:#155e75,color:#fff
ehai poc new booking "one-page booking with a week view"
ehai poc run booking 1                    # dev server on poc-1's own port
ehai poc iterate booking 1 "bigger time slots on mobile"
ehai poc run booking 2 -- pnpm test       # any command inside poc-2
ehai poc compare booking 1 2              # side-by-side report
ehai poc promote booking 2                # PR to main, after you confirm

You can also just ask your AI tool, for example "make a POC of a week view for booking". It calls ehai's poc_new tool for you.

AI-DLC's poc scope vs. ehai POCs

They complement each other. AI-DLC's poc scope runs a short lifecycle to prove an idea. ehai POCs are UI/UX variants of the app you already have, side by side in isolated worktrees, so you can compare and pick one before writing the spec.

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• One source of truth for each thing. Keep requirements and designs in the spec tool's files, and status, owners and bugs on the ehai board. Don't edit tasks in both places; re-run /ehai:breakdown → /ehai:sync when the spec changes.
  • Hand off early. Sync once the requirements and tasks are approved, not after the code is done, so the board shows real progress.
  • Same AI tool for both. Run ehai init once; ehai's commands then appear next to the spec tool's in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot and others.
  • Sensitive data: the data policy guard checks everything ehai writes to the tracker, including text taken from spec files.

docs.title: Use Cases
docs.text: Real workflows with ehai, organized by role.

docs.title: Use case 1 — New feature from idea to tracker in one session
docs.text:
Scenario: A PM has a vague feature idea and needs to turn it into a structured GitHub Project with epics, stories, and acceptance criteria.

Without ehai: 30-60 minutes writing a PRD in Notion, then manually creating 10-20 GitHub issues with the right labels, fields, and cross-links.

With ehai (Claude Code or Claude Desktop):

/ehai:plan  Users need to control which push notifications they receive

ehai: What problem does this solve?
PM:   Users complain about too many irrelevant notifications

ehai: Who are the main user types?
PM:   Mobile users (iOS and Android), PM users

ehai: What does success look like in 30 days?
PM:   50% of active users update their notification preferences
      Notification-related support tickets drop 20%

[ehai produces full PRD with Mermaid user flows]
[gap-finder runs: "No error/edge case flow — what happens when saving fails?"]

PM:   Show a toast and retry once automatically

/ehai:breakdown
[PRD → 3 epics, 11 stories, acceptance criteria for each story]

/ehai:sync
[11 items created in GitHub Projects · Status/Priority/Size fields set]

Total time: ~15 minutes. Zero manual copy-paste.

docs.title: Use case 2 — Daily standup status
docs.text:
/ehai:status

→ Notifications epic: 73% done (8/11 tasks)
→ Stale items (no update in 5 days): #34 "iOS silent push cert", #41 "Prefs persistence"
→ Open PRs: #22 "Toggle component" (3 days old, no review)
→ Risk: "iOS silent push cert expires in 14 days — assign #34 today"

The PM gets this in 2 seconds instead of checking GitHub Projects manually.

docs.title: Use case 3 — Bug triage during a sprint
docs.text:
/ehai:triage  "App crashes when user opens notification settings with an empty preference list"

ehai: Type: Bug  Priority: P1  Size: S

Similar existing items:
  #38 "Crash on empty prefs" — created 3 days ago

Is this the same issue or a new one?
  A. Same — link to #38
  B. New — create a separate item

PM: B

→ Created #51 "Crash on empty notification pref list"
   Linked to #38 as related issue
   Set P1, Size S, assigned to current sprint

docs.title: Use case 4 — PM on Claude Code CLI (no Claude Desktop)
docs.text:
PMs who prefer the terminal get the same experience:

# in any terminal with Claude Code
claude
> /ehai:plan  A settings screen for notification preferences

ehai detects the PM role (set at ehai init) and formats output for non-technical readers: plain-language summaries, Mermaid diagrams inline, and an auto-opened HTML report at ~/.ehai/reports/.

docs.title: Use case 5 — Start a task without context-switching
docs.text:
Planned

/ehai:start is not built yet (spec §5.3). Today, take the task with /ehai:assign I'll take #42 and create the branch yourself. This shows the intended flow.

/ehai:start #42

→ Branch feat/42-notification-toggle created from main
→ Task loaded: "Notification Toggle Component"
   Acceptance criteria:
   - Given I open Settings > Notifications
   - When I toggle a category off
   - Then push notifications stop arriving for that category within 60 seconds
→ Card #42 set to In Progress

The developer now has the branch, the full acceptance criteria, and the design notes in context — without leaving their AI harness.

docs.title: Use case 6 — Open a PR with a generated description
docs.text:
Planned

/ehai:pr is not built yet (spec §5.3). This shows the intended flow.

/ehai:pr

→ PR title: "feat(notifications): add notification category toggle"
→ Body:
   ## Summary
   Implements the notification toggle component from #42.

   ## Acceptance criteria
   - [x] Toggle updates user preference via API
   - [x] Change takes effect within 60 seconds
   - [ ] Offline state handled (shows retry toast)

→ Card #42 moved to In Review

The PR links the issue, maps the diff to the acceptance criteria, and surfaces any unverified criteria so the reviewer knows what to focus on.

docs.title: Use case 7 — Build an isolated UI prototype
docs.text:
Scenario: Trying out two visual approaches for the notification settings screen before committing to one.

ehai poc new notifications "notification settings screen"

→ Created poc-1 on branch ehai/poc/notifications/poc-1
→ Worktree: ~/.ehai/worktrees/my-app/notifications/poc-1
→ Design tokens extracted: Tailwind config, NativeWind theme
→ .env copied, node_modules linked, port 3042 allocated

ehai poc run notifications 1

→ Dev server started at http://localhost:3042 (no cd needed)

ehai poc iterate notifications 1 "Make the section headers sticky and add an 'All Off' button"

→ poc-2 created (lineage: poc-1), port 3043

ehai poc compare notifications 1 2

→ Side-by-side comparison report opened in the browser

POCs are CLI commands (and poc_* MCP tools your AI harness can call); there are no /ehai:poc slash commands.

Neither poc-1 nor poc-2 touched main. The source repo's working tree is byte-identical to before.

To run a POC yourself, stay in the repo root; there's no need to find or cd into the worktree:

ehai poc run notifications 2              # dev server for poc-2, on its own port
ehai poc run notifications 2 -- pnpm test # any command inside poc-2
ehai poc shell notifications 2            # a shell inside poc-2 (`exit` to leave)

Each reply ends with a footer like this one:

★ Insights ─────────────────────────────────────
  Start it:      ehai poc run notifications 2
  Shell there:   ehai poc shell notifications 2
  Note: main is untouched; nothing is merged until you `ehai poc promote`.
────────────────────────────────────────────────

docs.title: Use case 8 — Monorepo with multiple apps
docs.text:
ehai detects the monorepo structure at ehai repo init:

Detected: pnpm monorepo
  apps/web      → Vite React (Tailwind CSS)
  apps/mobile   → React Native (NativeWind, Expo Router)
  services/api  → Go (Gin)

Which app does this POC target?
  A. apps/web
  B. apps/mobile

Each POC worktree gets the right .env, package manager, and port set for its app — including RCT_METRO_PORT isolation for React Native's Metro bundler.

docs.title: Use case 9 — Shared PRD and breakdown across PM and devs
docs.text:
The PM creates the PRD and breakdown in Claude Desktop. The sync writes items to GitHub Projects. Developers use Claude Code to pick up those items:

Dev: /ehai:assign I'll take #47
     → #47 "Notification API endpoint" assigned to you
     → Acceptance criteria are on the card: POST /users/me/notification-prefs accepts JSON…

/ehai:next (suggest the next task) and /ehai:start (branch + status) are planned and will automate this step.

The PM's planning work flows directly into the developer's context. No copy-paste, no Slack messages asking "what does this ticket mean?".

docs.title: Use case 10 — Data policy guard across the team
docs.text:
A developer accidentally pastes a real user email into a task comment:

Dev: Add a comment to #51: "Reported by jane.smith@company.com"
     (the harness calls ehai's comment_task tool)

ehai: Sensitive data detected: email ×1
      How should ehai handle this?
      A. Redact → "Reported by [REDACTED:email]"
      B. Keep as-is
      C. Cancel

Dev: A

→ Comment posted: "Reported by [REDACTED:email]"
→ Audit log: { "command": "comment_task", "action": "redact", "findings": [{"kind":"email","count":1}] }

The email never reaches GitHub. The audit log records what happened without storing the value.

docs.title: Use case 11 — Triage incoming issues faster
docs.text:
Connect ehai to your open-source project tracker and triage issues from your AI harness:

/ehai:triage  "Build fails on Windows with MSVC: error C2440 in src/util.rs"

→ Type: Bug  Priority: P2  Size: M
→ Tags: platform:windows, build
→ Similar: #89 "Windows CI failure on MSVC" (closed 2 weeks ago — may be related)

Is this new or the same?
  A. New  B. Duplicate of #89

→ Created #124, assigned "help wanted" label

docs.title: Adapting ehai to your workflow
docs.text:
Change your role

ehai config set user.role pm      # pm | dev | both

Rename all commands

# in ~/.ehai/config.toml
[brand]
name = "acme"

ehai adapters regenerate    # all slash commands become /acme:plan, /acme:start, etc.

Multiple trackers / projects

ehai tracker set github              # switch to GitHub Projects
ehai tracker set local               # switch to local store (offline)

Offline mode

The local tracker (ehai tracker set local) supports all PM flows — plan, breakdown, status, triage — with no network required. Use it for internal planning, pre-sales work, or when GitHub is unavailable.

docs.title: Plan — project-admin roles and the team list
docs.text: Status: approved · 2026-11-17

docs.title: Why
docs.text:
• Roles follow real authority. Whoever administers the GitHub project is the PM side; everyone else is a developer. Only admins choose their role (pm, dev or both); non-admins become dev automatically, with no question.
  • The team list powers collaboration: assigning and reassigning tasks, taking your own, and @mentioning people. It's cached so ehai doesn't ask GitHub every time.

docs.title: Decisions (from your answers)
docs.text:
Topic Decision Who is "admin" ProjectV2.viewerCanClose is true (GitHub lets only project admins close a project); the owner of a personal project is always admin No project connected yet dev; the role question appears once they connect a project they administer Team Repo assignable users ∪ org members (org-owned projects), merged by login and marked assignable PM-only actions None. Everyone can do everything. The role sets the experience (tone, suggested flows, defaults), not permissions; GitHub permissions stay the real gate Cache Filled on the first GitHub call, auto-refreshed when older than 24 h, ehai team refresh anytime

Assumption to confirm: "control the env" means the role is managed (admins choose, others are dev), not that ehai blocks devs from anything.

docs.title: 1. Role resolution — ehai-core + CLI
docs.text:
• New config section, written by ehai rather than by hand: 
    [access]
project_admin = true          # last check
checked = "2026-11-17"
  • Effective role:
  • Admin: the chosen role (pm / dev / both). Once the project is connected, the default is pm.
  • Non-admin or no project: dev.
  • A session override (EHAI_ROLE) only applies to admins, so it can't be used to bypass the rule.
  • When admin is checked (one cheap GraphQL call):
  • init, after the tracker step. The tracker question now comes before the role question, and the role question is shown only to admins.
  • tracker set, after connecting. Admins are asked for a role if they don't have one; non-admins see "You're a developer on project".
  • The daily team refresh and ehai team refresh. If someone loses admin, they're downgraded to dev with a one-line notice. If they gain it, they're told they can choose (ehai role set).
  • New commands:
  • ehai role shows the role and why ("admin of jagadeeshm007 #2 → chose pm").
  • ehai role set pm|dev|both is for admins; others get a clear explanation.
  • doctor shows the role, why it applies, and the team cache age.
  • The ehai://prefs resource adds role_source and project_admin, so skills phrase things correctly.

docs.title: 2. Team list — ehai-tracker::team
docs.text:
• GitHub queries (read-only):
  • repository.assignableUsers (paginated: login, name, node id)
  • organization.membersWithRole, only when the project owner is an org (needs read:org, which you have)
  • ProjectV2.viewerCanClose, fetched in the same request
  • Merged member: { login, name, id, assignable: bool, sources: [repo, org] }.
  • Cache file: ~/.ehai/cache/team/<owner>-<project>.json, holding { fetched_at, viewer, viewer_is_admin, members[] }.
  • Written atomically under a lock.
  • When it's stale, a refresh runs. If the refresh fails, ehai keeps using the old list and warns.
  • CLI: ehai team lists members and the cache age; ehai team refresh forces a fetch and also re-checks admin.

docs.title: 3. Assigning and mentions — tracker + MCP
docs.text:
• Tracker trait gains:
  • assign(id, logins) and unassign(id, logins)
  • Item.assignees
  • GitHub implementation:
  • Issues use addAssigneesToAssignable / removeAssigneesFromAssignable, with user node ids from the team cache.
  • Draft items use their own assignee update. I'll verify by schema introspection before building it.
  • Mentions: comment(id, body) stays the same; mention lists are added as @login … at the top.
  • New MCP tools:
  • team lists members, with an optional refresh.
  • assign_task:
    • It takes { item, assignees[], mode: add | replace | remove }.
    • item accepts #18, a URL, an ehai id, or a title fragment; "me" means the caller.
    • If a name is unknown or ambiguous, or the item is ambiguous, it returns needs_input with team or item options.
    • It warns when someone isn't assignable on the repo.
  • comment_task posts a comment with optional mentions.
  • Plans:
  • Stories and tasks get an optional assignees field.
  • Assignees are set when an item is created. After that the board owns them, like status, so a re-sync never undoes a reassignment.
  • The breakdown preview gets an "Assignee" column.
  • Triage: an optional assignee.
  • Status report:
  • A "By person" table (open / in progress / done per assignee).
  • New risk flags: in-progress work with nobody assigned, and anyone with more than 5 items in progress.

docs.title: 4. Skills and prompts
docs.text:
• New /ehai:assign ("assign #18 to Priya", "I'll take #19", "move #20 from Ravi to Asha"). It asks through the question tool, offering team members as options.
  • breakdown suggests assignees from the team (optional). status shows the per-person table. triage can assign.
  • init's "Try next" card and help change by role: PMs see plan, breakdown and status; devs see assign/take, status and triage.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
• Fake GitHub:
  • viewerCanClose switchable per test
  • assignable users and org members
  • assign and unassign mutations
  • assignees in items
  • Contract suite: assign/unassign round-trip on the memory and GitHub trackers; unknown login → error.
  • Role:
  • Admin is asked the role; non-admin gets no question and dev.
  • No project → dev.
  • Losing admin on refresh downgrades; role set is refused for non-admins.
  • EHAI_ROLE is ignored for non-admins.
  • init with a non-admin asks one question fewer.
  • Team cache: first call fills it; a fresh cache makes no network call; a stale one refreshes; a failed refresh keeps the old list.
  • MCP: assign_task covers "me", replace and remove, an ambiguous name (needs_input), an unassignable user (warning), and by-person status numbers.
  • Live (opt-in): on aisdlc-demo, assign #19 to yourself, unassign, and post a mention comment. The non-admin path can only be tested on the fake, because you administer everything here.

docs.title: Out of scope (later)
docs.text:
• Notifying people outside GitHub (Slack, email).
  • Workload-based assignment suggestions (M6, preference learning).
  • The developer flow (/ehai:next, start, pr, done; planned, not built yet) builds on this: next will prefer tasks assigned to you.

docs.title: Deliverable
docs.text:
• One commit: feat: project-admin roles, team list, task assignment.
  • Docs updated (README, PROGRESS, a DECISIONS ADR).
  • Everything above tested, plus the live assign check on aisdlc-demo.

docs.title: Config Reference
docs.text:
ehai uses TOML configuration with a layered merge. Narrower layers win:

defaults < ~/.ehai/config.toml < .ehai.toml (repo) < --config flag < EHAI_SECTION__KEY env < CLI flags

docs.title: [brand]
docs.text:
[brand]
name = "ehai"   # rename the binary and all slash commands; default "ehai"

After changing name, run ehai adapters regenerate to re-render all installed harness files.

docs.title: [compliance]
docs.text:
[compliance]
mode    = "warn"    # off | warn | strict
profile = "tech"    # tech | health | finance | gdpr
patterns = []       # custom patterns appended after profile rules

patterns schema:

[[compliance.patterns]]
name  = "employee-id"           # used in [REDACTED:name] notices
regex = "\\bEMP-\\d{6}\\b"     # Rust regex syntax

See Data Policy guide for profile details.

docs.text:

mode = "restricted"   # off | restricted | container
Mode What it restricts off No restrictions restricted (default) POC agents write only inside their worktree and ~/.ehai/; destructive commands blocked container POC dev servers run in Docker/Podman; requires a container runtime

channel = "alpha"   # alpha | beta | stable
auto    = false     # true: auto-install in background (default: notify only)

docs.title: [tracker]

docs.title: [env]
docs.text:
Controls worktree environment provisioning (POC engine and ehai env sync):

[env]
strategy      = "copy"     # copy | symlink
include       = []         # extra glob patterns to copy (e.g. "apps/*/.env*")
exclude       = []         # patterns to skip (e.g. ".env.production")
install_deps  = true       # run package manager install in each worktree
rn_native     = false      # pod install / Gradle (slow; opt-in)

[env.smoke]
web = "pnpm -C apps/web typecheck"
api = "go build ./..."

docs.title: [log]

docs.title: Environment variable overrides
docs.text:
Any config key can be overridden with EHAI_<SECTION>__<KEY>:

EHAI_COMPLIANCE__MODE=strict ehai init
EHAI_UPDATE__CHANNEL=beta ehai update

Values are parsed as TOML literals (true, 42, "string").

docs.title: MCP Tools Reference
docs.text:
ehai exposes an MCP server (ehai mcp) with the following tools. All tools are available in every connected harness.

When a tool returns "status": "needs_input", the harness's question UI shows the prompt; call the same tool again with retry_param set to the chosen value.

docs.title: Core
docs.text: Tool Description ping Health check — returns {"ok": true, "version": "…"}

docs.title: PM flow
docs.text: Tool Key params Description save_prd title, content, slug?, policy? Store a PRD; runs the data-policy guard before writing get_plan slug Retrieve a saved PRD by slug list_plans — List all saved PRDs with slug, title, created_at save_breakdown slug, breakdown, policy? Store an epic/story/task breakdown linked to a PRD slug sync_plan slug Push the breakdown to the connected tracker, idempotently status_report slug? Progress report: % done per epic, blockers, stale items, open PRs triage report, policy? Classify a bug/request → tracker item with duplicate detection plan_explore slug, round? Gap-finder iteration: surfaces unanswered questions in a PRD draft

docs.title: Developer flow
docs.text: Tool Key params Description comment_task item_id, body, policy? Post a comment on a tracker item assign_task item_id, assignee Assign a tracker item to a team member

docs.title: Team
docs.text: Tool Key params Description team action (list/add/remove) Manage the team roster (GitHub assignable users, with cache)

docs.title: Guard
docs.text: Tool Key params Description guard_check text, mode? Scan a string for sensitive data; returns findings with kind and count. Values are never stored.

docs.title: Resources
docs.text: Resource URI Description ehai://prefs Current user role and learned preferences as a compact JSON block

docs.title: Sensitive data policy param (policy)
docs.text:
Tools that write content accept an optional policy field to answer a pending sensitive-data question:

{
  "tool": "save_prd",
  "args": {
    "slug": "notifications",
    "content": "…",
    "policy": "redact"   // "redact" | "keep" | "cancel"
  }
}

If a tool finds sensitive data and policy is not set, it returns needs_input with a question for the user. Set policy on the retry call to proceed.

docs.title: Skills Reference
docs.text:
Skills are the user-facing layer over ehai's MCP tools. Each skill is a slash command (/ehai:<name>) that handles the multi-turn question loop, calls the right tools in order, and formats output for your role.

Skills are installed per-harness by ehai connect <harness> or ehai init. They are plain text templates that instruct the AI how to call the MCP tools.

docs.title: /ehai:plan
docs.text:
When to use: When you have an idea, a feature request, or a problem statement and need to produce a full PRD.

What it does:

  1. Asks 3–5 clarifying questions using multiple-choice where possible (problem, users, goals, scope, success metrics)
  2. Produces a PRD with Mermaid user flows, risks, out-of-scope list
  3. Calls plan_explore in a loop (up to 3 rounds) to surface gaps — missing metrics, missing edge cases, no out-of-scope list
  4. Asks for your approval before save_prd writes anything

Usage:

/ehai:plan [optional initial description]

If you provide an initial description, ehai skips the first question and starts with that as the problem statement.

Output: PRD document (Markdown + Mermaid). In Claude Desktop it writes a Claude Doc. In CLI harnesses it writes docs/prd/<slug>.md in your repo.

MCP tools called: plan_explore, save_prd

docs.title: /ehai:breakdown
docs.text:
When to use: After a PRD is saved. Turns the PRD into work items.

What it does:

  1. Reads the saved PRD (calls get_plan)
  2. Generates epics → stories → tasks with Given/When/Then acceptance criteria
  3. Assigns priority (P0–P3), size (XS–XL), and platform tags (web, mobile, api)
  4. Shows a board preview and waits for your approval
  5. Calls save_breakdown to persist

Usage:

/ehai:breakdown [prd slug, optional — uses latest if omitted]

MCP tools called: get_plan, save_breakdown

docs.title: /ehai:sync
docs.text:
When to use: After a breakdown is saved and you're ready to push to your tracker.

What it does:

  1. First runs a dry-run (apply: false) to show what would change: N items to create, M items to update
  2. Waits for confirmation
  3. Pushes with apply: true — idempotent: re-running never duplicates items

Usage:

/ehai:sync [prd slug, optional]

Idempotency: Each synced item gets an ehai-id written to its tracker body footer. Subsequent runs diff local vs remote by that ID, never creating duplicates.

MCP tools called: sync_plan

docs.title: /ehai:status
docs.text:
When to use: At any point to get a progress snapshot across all epics.

What it does:

  1. Calls status_report (fetches from tracker)
  2. Formats: % done per epic, stale items, open PRs, risk flags
  3. Outputs Markdown + Mermaid progress diagram
  4. Optionally writes an HTML report to ~/.ehai/reports/

Usage:

/ehai:status [--html]

MCP tools called: status_report

docs.title: /ehai:triage
docs.text:
When to use: When a bug is reported, a user request comes in, or an issue needs to be turned into a tracker item.

What it does:

  1. If the report is vague, asks at most 3 questions: what happened vs expected, how often, where
  2. Classifies type (Bug/Story/Task), priority (P0–P3), size (XS–XL)
  3. Checks for duplicates against existing items
  4. If a possible duplicate is found, asks: same issue or new?
  5. Creates the tracker item

Priority guide: - P0 — Critical impact, no workaround - P1 — Major impact, workaround exists - P2 — Minor impact - P3 — Cosmetic

Usage:

/ehai:triage [description]

MCP tools called: triage

docs.title: /ehai:assign
docs.text:
When to use: To assign, reassign, or take a task.

Usage:

/ehai:assign  #42 to priya
/ehai:assign  "notification toggle" to me
/ehai:assign  #42 remove jagadeesh

MCP tools called: assign_task, team

docs.title: /ehai:prefs
docs.text:
When to use: To view or edit your role and learned preferences.

What it shows: - Your current role (pm / dev / both) - High-confidence learned preferences (planning style, POC taste, estimate scale) - Recent observations

Usage:

/ehai:prefs
/ehai:prefs set role dev
/ehai:prefs delete planning.granularity

MCP tools called: ehai://prefs resource

docs.title: /ehai:next
docs.text:
When to use: When you want to know what to work on next.

What it does: Suggests the next unblocked task by priority, assignee, and dependency order.

Usage:

/ehai:next

MCP tools called: status_report

docs.title: /ehai:start
docs.text:
When to use: When picking up a task. Creates the branch and loads context.

What it does:

  1. Looks up the item in the tracker (by number, URL, or partial title)
  2. Creates feat/<id>-<slug> branch from main
  3. Loads the task's full context (acceptance criteria, description, linked PRD)
  4. Sets the card to In Progress

Usage:

/ehai:start #42
/ehai:start notification toggle

MCP tools called: assign_task (sets to In Progress)

docs.title: /ehai:pr
docs.text:
When to use: When you're ready to open a pull request.

What it does:

  1. Reads the current branch name and infers the linked task number
  2. Generates a PR description that:
  3. Links the issue (Fixes #42)
  4. Maps each acceptance criterion to a checkbox
  5. Flags any unverified criteria
  6. Shows the draft and waits for approval
  7. After PR is opened, moves the card to In Review

Usage:

/ehai:pr

MCP tools called: comment_task (after PR created externally)

docs.title: /ehai:done
docs.text:
When to use: When a PR is merged and the task is complete.

What it does: Verifies acceptance criteria are satisfied (asks if any are unchecked) and moves the card to Done.

Usage:

/ehai:done [#id, defaults to current branch task]

MCP tools called: assign_task (sets to Done)

docs.title: POC commands
docs.text: POCs are driven from the ehai poc CLI, and the same operations are exposed as poc_* MCP tools your harness can call. There are no /ehai:poc slash commands. <feature> is a short slug (e.g. notifications); <n> is the POC number.

docs.title: ehai poc new
docs.text:
When to use: When you want to prototype a UI feature without touching main.

What it does:

  1. Extracts design tokens from your repo (Tailwind, NativeWind, MUI themes, etc.)
  2. Creates an isolated git worktree at ~/.ehai/worktrees/<repo>/<feature>/poc-<n> on branch ehai/poc/<feature>/poc-<n>
  3. Provisions the worktree: copies .env*, installs dependencies, allocates a unique port
  4. Registers the POC in the manifest and prints the worktree, port, URL and design context
ehai poc new notifications "notification settings screen"

MCP tool: poc_new

docs.title: ehai poc iterate
docs.text:
When to use: To refine an existing POC with feedback.

ehai poc iterate notifications 1 "Make the section headers sticky and add an All Off button"

Creates the next POC (e.g. poc-2) with lineage pointing to poc-1. Both POCs remain accessible.

MCP tool: poc_iterate

docs.title: ehai poc compose
docs.text:
When to use: To synthesize a new POC that takes the best parts of multiple earlier ones.

What it does: Starts from the base branch; the AI reads the referenced POCs' diffs and resynthesizes the described parts — not a blind cherry-pick. Lineage records each parent.

ehai poc compose notifications "Take the sticky headers from poc-1 and the toggle design from poc-2" --from 1 --from 2

MCP tool: poc_compose

docs.title: ehai poc list
docs.text:
ehai poc list
ehai poc list notifications      # filter by feature

docs.title: ehai poc compare
docs.text:
ehai poc compare notifications 1 2

Writes a side-by-side HTML comparison report and opens it in the browser.

docs.title: ehai poc open
docs.text:
ehai poc open notifications 2

Prints the worktree path, dev-server command and URL for the POC.

docs.title: ehai poc run / ehai poc shell
docs.text:
When to use: to start a POC or run any command in it without cd-ing into its worktree. Works from anywhere inside the repo.

ehai poc run checkout 2                 # start the detected dev server
ehai poc run checkout 2 -- pnpm test    # any command, inside the worktree
ehai poc shell checkout 2               # your shell, inside the worktree; `exit` to come back

Commands run in ~/.ehai/worktrees/<repo>/<feature>/poc-<n> with that worktree's .env.ehai.local loaded, so each POC uses its own ports (PORT, COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME, …). The exit code is passed through, so ehai poc run … -- pnpm test works in scripts. ehai poc shell also sets EHAI_POC=<feature>/poc-<n>, which you can show in your prompt.

docs.title: ehai poc promote
docs.text:
When to use: When you've chosen a POC and want to open a PR to merge it.

Safety: Always asks for confirmation (--yes does not skip it). The POC branch is never merged silently.

ehai poc promote notifications 2

docs.title: ehai poc discard
docs.text:
ehai poc discard notifications 1

Archives the POC as branch ehai-archive/<feature>/poc-1 and removes the worktree. Nothing is hard-deleted.

docs.title: Customizing skills
docs.text:
Skills are plain text files. After connecting a harness, they live in the harness's prompt/command directory. To customize:

  1. Find the file: ehai adapters list shows the installed paths.
  2. Edit the template outside the # >>> ehai >>> ... # <<< ehai <<< markers.
  3. Changes inside the markers are overwritten by ehai adapters regenerate.

To rename all slash commands to a custom prefix:

# ~/.ehai/config.toml
[brand]
name = "acme"

ehai adapters regenerate    # all skills become /acme:plan, /acme:start, etc.

docs.title: User Preference Agent Design
docs.text: ehai learns how each user and repo works over time and injects that knowledge into every tool call, so later interactions need fewer questions and produce better-tailored output by default.

docs.title: What ehai already has
docs.text:
The ehai://prefs MCP resource is loaded at the start of every skill invocation. It reflects ~/.ehai/prefs/user.toml at call time — there is no in-memory session state to sync. The AI sees a compact "User preferences" block such as:

planning_style: detailed
last_plan_complexity: 7
poc_created: true

Preferences have a source (explicit = user-stated, observed = inferred from behavior), a confidence (0.0–1.0), and timestamps. Explicit statements always beat observations. Confidence decays if a preference is not reinforced; contradicting evidence lowers it.

docs.title: Maintaining context across sessions
docs.text: The MCP resource is stateless by design: it reads the TOML file on every call. The AI does not need to "remember" across sessions because the prefs file is the persistent memory. No special session handoff is required; ehai://prefs always reflects the latest state.

docs.title: Progressive signal gathering
docs.text:
After every significant interaction, MCP tools call a private observe_interaction helper on EhaiServer. It is fire-and-forget: errors are silently ignored so a prefs write failure never breaks the main flow.

fn observe_interaction(&self, key: &str, value: &str) {
    let mut prefs = Prefs::load_global(&self.ctx.home).unwrap_or_default();
    prefs.set(key, value, Scope::Global, Source::Observed);
    let _ = prefs.save_global(&self.ctx.home);
}

Current observation points:

Tool Key Value save_prd last_plan_complexity count of risks + flows as a string poc_new poc_created "true"

Candidates for future wiring: - plan_explore returning 0 gaps → requirements_completeness: thorough - Three or more poc_iterate calls on the same feature → poc_iteration_depth: deep - Consistent story-point scale chosen → estimate_scale: fibonacci

docs.title: Compaction
docs.text:
When the prefs file grows beyond 50 entries, save_global runs a compaction pass automatically:

  1. Keep all entries where source == explicit (user-stated facts are never dropped).
  2. Keep the top-30 observed entries, sorted by key (deterministic across machines).
  3. Write the compacted set back.

This bounds the file at roughly 50–60 entries indefinitely.

docs.title: Privacy guarantee
docs.text:
Observation keys and values describe behavioral patterns only — they never contain PHI. The PHI guard (ehai-guard) does not need to scan this file because:

  • Keys are hard-coded strings in source ("last_plan_complexity", "poc_created").
  • Values are counts, booleans, or enum-like labels — never user-entered free text.
  • The prefs file is never sent to the tracker, included in reports, or read by the LLM as raw content (only the compact to_context_text() block is injected).

Values are never logged in compliance findings — only kinds and counts.

docs.title: Two scopes
docs.text:
Scope File Committed? Global (user) ~/.ehai/prefs/user.toml No — machine-local Repo (project) <repo>/.ehai/prefs/project.toml Configurable

Resolution order: explicit repo decision > explicit user preference > observed repo convention > observed user preference > defaults.

docs.title: User control
docs.text: ehai prefs list — show all entries with source, confidence, and timestamps. ehai prefs set <key> <value> — write an explicit entry that beats all observations. ehai prefs delete <key> — remove an entry. prefs.learning = false in config — disable all observation writes globally.
